title: Copy and claims
description: Text that sounds like a person who knows the product, makes only claims it can support and moves the reader to act.

criteria.title: Specific, not generic
criteria.ask: Replace the product name with a competitor's: does each sentence still read true? Concrete nouns, numbers and examples win.
criteria.evidence: Three before/after rewrites that replaced a generic line with a specific one.

criteria.title: Every claim is supportable
criteria.ask: Best, fastest, secure, trusted-by, guaranteed, AI-powered: can each be shown?
criteria.evidence: Each claim with its source, or the safer wording that replaced it.

criteria.title: One consistent voice
criteria.ask: Same person speaking on every page, in the language the audience uses?
criteria.evidence: A voice description and the places checked.

criteria.title: Clear structure
criteria.ask: Can a skimmer get the point from headings and first lines alone?
criteria.evidence: The heading outline read on its own.

criteria.title: No machine tells
criteria.ask: Staged run-ups, forced triples, inflated significance, 'unlock/elevate/seamless', symmetric filler?

criteria.title: Calls to action match intent
criteria.ask: Does each button say what happens next, and is there one primary action per view?

criteria.title: Titles and descriptions
criteria.ask: Unique titles and descriptions that match the page, without keyword stuffing?
